title: Defensive Network and System Security
summary: Connect secure configuration, permissions, monitoring, and segmentation concepts.
objectives: Describe how segmentation can reduce unnecessary access.

vocab.def: Separating systems or network areas to control access and limit impact.
A control that allows or denies traffic according to defined rules.
Applying approved updates to address maintenance or security needs.

sections.heading: Reduce unnecessary paths
sections.body: Least privilege, approved patching, backups, monitoring, secure configuration, and segmentation can reduce risk. Scenarios use simulated systems only.

sections.heading: Authorized diagnostics
sections.body: Do not evade firewalls, exploit services, scan external networks, intercept traffic, or access systems outside the defined lab scope.

practice.prompt: Why might a lab separate management systems from general endpoints?
practice.answer: Segmentation can reduce unnecessary access and limit the impact of a problem.

quiz.question: What is a defensive use of segmentation?
options: Control unnecessary access between system areas
quiz.answer: Control unnecessary access between system areas

lab.objective: Interpret a synthetic segmented system model.

reflectionPrompt: What authorization would be needed before a configuration change?
